newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FOCUS - Swiss Winterthur profits up.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Swiss Winterthur profits up.

text.p: Swiss insurance giant Winterthur Insurance Co on Tuesday reported a one-fourth increase in its first half group net profit and forecast a double-digit growth rate for full-year profits.

In its first complete interim report, Winterthur said first half profits rose to 248.4 million Swiss francs ($198 million). But it omitted a figure for first half 1995 profits saying it would not be accurate comparison.
Chairman and chief executive Peter Spaelti, speaking at a news conference, put 1995's estimated half-year net profit at around 200 million francs.
Winterthur's strategy of focusing on core insurance business and higher profitability would continue to pay off in the next few years, he said.
"We will continuously increase profits in the next years and continuously raise the return on investments," he said.

"...the good results of the first six months forms a reliable basis on which to achieve another double-digit growth rate in profits in the current business year and a marked increase in shareholders equity by end 1996."
Dealers said the first half-year result was at the lower end of expectations. Winterthur's shares ended 11 francs lower at 763 francs on a slightly disappointed stock market.
Since 1992, when Winterthur began implementing its current strategy, annual profits have risen by an average 19.6 percent.
Spaelti said higher profits should mean a higher dividend, underscoring Winterthur's commitment to raise shareholder value.
"A double-digit profit growth would certainly have a positive effect on the dividend. This would mean a rise (in the dividend) similar to the previous year's," he said.
Winterthur raised dividend on 1995 results to 19 Swiss francs from 17 per share as net profit rose 15.1 percent to 419.2 million.
European operations excluding Switzerland were expected to drive profit growth in the next three to five years with substantial cost savings seen in Germany, Spain and Italy.
Over the next five to 10 years, profit growth will be driven by multinational industrial business and Asia-Pacific including China, where Winterthur has four representative offices.
In the multinational industrial business, Winterthur already cooperates with CS First Boston and Swiss Reinsurance.
It is concentrating on integrating recently acquired companies, rationalisation measures and increasing profits.

Improving the profitability of German, Spanish and Italian operations and boosting cooperation with Germany's Commerzbank, Switzerland's CS Holding and Belgium's Banque Bruxelles Lambert are among the current projects.
Spaelti saw insurance premiums up by around nine percent in 1996 to around 24 billion francs, similar to last year's rise. First half premiums rose 17 percent to 14.3 billion.
The company said its pool of investments should also rise in line with the expected premium growth in 1996 and balloon to almost 80 billion francs from 78.3 billion in mid-year.
Head of finance, Erwin Heri, said he was convinced another excellent financial result would be achieved this year.
First-half investment income of 2.78 billion Swiss francs was more or less in line with the budget, which foresees an increase of eight to 10 percent.
But Heri was cautious about the Swiss market. He said the Swiss equity market was not cheap. The economy had remained subdued and that would affect equity markets sooner or later.
-- Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340 ($1=1.2532 Swiss Franc)
